disease_label_per_paper: Aspiration pneumonia caused by fentanyl-induced cough during anesthesia induction

past_history: renal cell carcinoma scheduled for nephrectomy

presentation_summary: A 32-year-old man underwent anesthesia induction for hand-assisted laparoscopic left nephrectomy.
After fentanyl administration he suddenly coughed vigorously for about 30 seconds and vomited a large volume of greenish fluid around the face mask.
Greenish fluid was later suctioned from the endotracheal tube, and bronchoscopy found bile-stained fluid and undigested food particles in the trachea, right main bronchus, and lower lobar bronchi.
Oxygen saturation transiently dropped and then gradually fell to 92% after CO2 insufflation; ABG on FiO2 1.0 showed pH 7.334, PaO2 82.2 mmHg, PaCO2 44.2 mmHg, and bicarbonate 24.9 mEq/L.
Postoperative chest radiograph showed patchy consolidation in the right lower lung field and decreased right lung volume; fever to 38.6 C developed and antimicrobial therapy was started.

outcome_follow_up.description: Temperature normalized by the next day, chest radiograph improved, patient was extubated and transferred to the ward, and discharged home seven days after surgery.

quality_warnings: This is a peri-anesthesia witnessed macroaspiration case; the triggering fentanyl-induced cough is context, not part of the disease leaf name.
Treatment response and discharge outcome are non-ranking.
Bronchoscopy findings are preserved both as direct acute observation and as a non-ranking confirmatory finding.
